Section B: answer ALL 2 questions in this section using the spaces provided; both questions carry equal marks. Section C: answer ONLY TWO questions out of three; if you attempt more than 2 questions, only the first two will be considered. Where appropriate, equations and diagrams should be used to illustrate your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$.
enonce_intro_markdown: Particles in the following substances are held by different chemical bonds. You are given: sodium chloride (NaCl), Hydrogen gas ($\mathrm{H_2}$), and Aluminium metal (Al).

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the bond type in each substance and briefly explain, using diagrams if need be, how each chemical bond type is formed. *[14 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Sodium chloride, NaCl: ionic (electrovalent) bond.** A sodium atom (2, 8, 1) is a metal and **transfers its one outer electron** to a chlorine atom (2, 8, 7), a non-metal. Both obtain a full outer shell of 8 electrons:

$$
\mathrm{Na \rightarrow Na^+ + e^-} \qquad \mathrm{Cl + e^- \rightarrow Cl^-}
$$

The oppositely charged ions $\mathrm{Na^+}$ and $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ are held together by strong **electrostatic attraction** in a giant ionic lattice (each ion surrounded by ions of opposite charge).

**Hydrogen gas, $\mathrm{H_2}$: covalent bond.** Each hydrogen atom has one electron and needs a second to fill its shell (a duplet). Two hydrogen atoms (both non-metals) **share one pair of electrons**, so each atom has two electrons around it: $\mathrm{H} + \mathrm{H} \rightarrow \mathrm{H-H}$.

The shared pair is attracted by both nuclei and forms a single covalent bond. The molecules are small and separate.

**Aluminium metal, Al: metallic bond.** Each aluminium atom (2, 8, 3) gives up its **three outer electrons** to a common pool. The metal is a regular lattice of positive ions $\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$ surrounded by a "sea" of **delocalised electrons** that move freely. The attraction between the positive ions and the sea of electrons is the metallic bond.

*Diagrams expected:* dot and cross diagram showing the transfer of an electron from Na to Cl, with the ions in square brackets with their charges; dot and cross diagram of $\mathrm{H_2}$ with one shared pair; a lattice of $+$ ions in a sea of electrons for Al.

questions.enonce_markdown: State one physical property of each substance and relate this property to the bond type. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Substance (bond) | Physical property | Link with the bond type |
|---|---|---|
| NaCl (ionic) | **High melting point** ($801\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$); conducts electricity only when **molten or dissolved in water**, not as a solid | A lot of energy is needed to overcome the strong electrostatic attraction between the ions. The ions are fixed in the solid lattice, but become free to move when molten or dissolved, so they can carry current |
| $\mathrm{H_2}$ (covalent, simple molecules) | **Very low boiling point** (gas at room temperature); does **not conduct** electricity | The molecules are held to each other only by weak intermolecular forces, which need little energy to overcome; there are no ions or free electrons to carry current |
| Al (metallic) | **Good conductor of electricity** (and of heat); also malleable and ductile | The delocalised electrons are free to move through the lattice and carry the current; layers of ions can slide over one another without breaking the bonding |
